_readme: The writing systems as a tree over time (scripts/build-scripts.js, docs/writing-systems-plan.md). Each stage: its signs (strokes in a unit box, and an SVG path inked with its ductus), their values and what each came from; its changes, dated and named. The line and dates are placeholders for DJ to change.

painted.label: painted
painted.note: the first signs were pictures, drawn and painted before anyone cut them

incised.label: incised on bone
incised.note: a point on bone or wood cuts straight lines; curves become angles (Chinese oracle bone script, the runes)

chisel.label: cut in stone
chisel.note: a chisel likes straight cuts and leaves a small foot at each end (Roman capitals, early Greek)

stylus.label: pressed into clay
stylus.note: a reed stylus pressed into wet clay leaves a wedge at each push (cuneiform)

brush.label: brushed
brush.note: a brush thickens as it presses and thins as it lifts (Chinese regular script)

pen.label: reed pen
pen.note: a broad nib is thick across its edge and thin along it (Latin, Greek, Arabic hands)

leaf.label: on palm leaf
leaf.note: a point on a palm leaf must curve: a straight stroke splits the leaf (the round scripts of south India, Burma, Java)

stages.name: Alzurian proto-writing

changes.note: 96 signs drawn as pictures of the words they stand for
changes.analogue: Sumerian, Egyptian and Chinese writing each began as pictures of words: the Sumerian head, mouth, water and grain; the Egyptian owl, hand and reed

stages.note: pictures of words, painted and scratched: tallies and names on pots and seals (the wiki: Alzurian proto-writing, after Harappa)

changes.note: cut into bone with a point, the curves became angles
changes.analogue: the Chinese oracle bone script (c. 1200 BC): the brush-drawn pictures cut into bone come out angular

changes.note: each sign read for its sound as well as its word, so a picture could write any word that sounded like it
changes.analogue: Sumerian: the sign for "arrow" (ti) wrote "life" (ti); Egyptian and Chinese did the same

changes.note: 7 signs took a mark to be told from another
changes.analogue: the Arabic dots

changes.note: the signs turned a quarter when scribes turned from columns to lines written with a pen
changes.analogue: cuneiform signs turned a quarter when the tablet did (c. 2500 BC)

changes.note: written fast with a reed pen, strokes joined and corners rounded
changes.analogue: Egyptian hieratic beside the hieroglyphs; the Alzurian cursive the wiki names

changes.note: the small strokes dropped
changes.analogue: every cursive hand

changes.note: 2 signs took a mark to be told from another
changes.analogue: the Arabic dots
